developer: DermaSensor Inc. (founders include Dr. Maurice Ferre and Christopher Dewey). Company history describes development of Elastic Scattering Spectroscopy (ESS) and a proprietary machine learning algorithm trained on histopathology-confirmed lesions.
availability: FDA-cleared and available for sale in the U.S.; CE marked; waitlist/limited state availability described publicly.
summary: Connected handheld device intended to help frontline providers assess lesions suspicious for melanoma/BCC/SCC and inform referral decisions, producing results in seconds. Identified suspicious lesion is scanned with five spectral recordings; algorithm returns “Investigate Further” or “Monitor,” with a 1–10 similarity score for malignancy patterns. Intended for use alongside clinician assessment and not as a screening tool or sole diagnostic criterion.
medicalPurpose: Identified suspicious lesion is scanned with five spectral recordings; algorithm returns “Investigate Further” or “Monitor,” with a 1–10 similarity score for malignancy patterns. Intended for use alongside clinician assessment and not as a screening tool or sole diagnostic criterion.
acceptableInput: Spectral recordings from the scanned lesion. Input: spectral signal; Output: categorical result + numeric score intended to guide referral decisions. Three-step process (identify lesion → apply device/record spectra → receive result).
output: Output includes referral-oriented risk classification and score; intended to improve triage and reduce missed cancers by clinicians in reader studies.
roleInDecisionMaking: Provides adjunctive referral support for physicians evaluating suspicious lesions; does not replace clinician judgment, biopsy, or definitive diagnosis.
intendedUsers: Qualified healthcare professionals in clinical settings; marketed for non-dermatology providers in primary care and related outpatient settings. Clinical assessment skills for lesion selection and interpretation; device is an adjunct to clinical judgment.
targetPatientPopulation: Patients (often 40+) with lesions already judged suspicious for melanoma/BCC/SCC where a referral decision is being considered.
unsupportedUseCases: Not for screening or unsupervised population triage. Not the sole basis for diagnosis or referral decisions.
requiredClinicianOversight: Independent clinical assessment, including visual lesion evaluation, is required before and alongside device use. Definitive diagnosis requires clinician judgment and biopsy or pathology confirmation where clinically indicated.
modelType: AI/ML classifier analyzing Elastic Scattering Spectroscopy (ESS) recordings from intact skin lesions.

clinicalTrial.description: Study evidence and summaries described in the clinical evidence PDF.

performance.summary: Public materials and study summaries report no device-related safety issues; primary safety concerns are clinical consequences of false results. Human-in-the-loop clinical judgment remains required; device should be used only as intended.

ongoingMonitoringPlan: Algorithm is described as “locked” with periodic revalidation/updates requiring FDA clearance.
